newsitem.title: FINLAND: Profit-takers knock Helsinki off record best.
newsitem.headline: Profit-takers knock Helsinki off record best.

text.p: Shares closed a shade higher on Tuesday amid strength in financial, engineering and small cap stocks after late profit-taking mainly in bourse engine Nokia hit the market and shook up the compass, brokers said.

The HEX set a new 2,900.36 point record in early trade as Nokia headed higher, but then retreated and reports of a downgrade from Natwest and an Ericsson expectation of sharp GSM price erosion this year hit Nokia and further trimmed the index.
The HEX ended at 2,865.82, up 0.08 percent, with volume at 940 million markka -- almost a typical level since the turn of the year but about three times the daily average of 1996.
Nokia made up 40 percent of total volume and fell 2.20 markka to 306.
Brokers said the market would digest the news, and one plotted a test of support for Nokia around 300 markka. "I'd start buying just above 300," he said.
Nokia earlier hit 316.00 markka, recovering after U.S. profit-takers took it below 310.00 on Friday in the wake of Thursday's in-line 1996 report.
"U.S. investors seem again to be taking profits from Nokia as they did on Friday," one broker said. But another said the stock was sold by traders rather than investors.

In financials, merger activity continued in Sweden with Swedbank and Foreningsbanken, keeping Finnish financials on the boil. The insurance sub-index rose 1.22 percent, led by Sampo's 10.00 markka rise to 447.00.
But Finland's largest bank Merita closed flat at 18.70, holding recent gains.
Cyclical shares were supported by the strong dollar but forestries ended in negative ground as UPM pared recent gains, down 1.50 markka at 105.00 in massive trade.
Paper machine maker Valmet accounted for six percent of volume as it rose 1.00 markka to close at 95.00.
